statusText: Roughly six hours into the U.S. cash session, the Nasdaq-100 complex continues to hold its advance: the S&P 500 sits at a fresh record above 7,800 and the Nasdaq Composite remains higher on the day, with semiconductor-led breadth (Sandisk, Micron) intact alongside continued strength in megacap tech. A flat July PPI print continues to reinforce Wednesday's benign CPI and reduced Fed-hike odds, while WTI crude holds its slide, down roughly 1.4% to about $81-82. Alpha Vantage's free-tier daily budget remains fully exhausted this run -- a second TREASURY_YIELD attempt was again rejected with a rate_limit error -- so this assessment again leans on web reporting alone; VIX and the 10-year Treasury yield are carried forward from Wednesday's close rather than confirmed intraday. No failed-pullback or repeated-extension price action has been identified, so Tail stays low. Stress builds toward the moderate band's upper edge as the session approaches its 20:00 UTC close and Applied Materials' 20:30 UTC earnings call, where the options market is now pricing an implied ~11% move -- nearly double the stock's ~6% average post-earnings reaction over the last four quarters. headline: Nasdaq-100 holds its record-high push -- S&P 500 above 7,800 with semiconductor-led breadth intact -- as Alpha Vantage's daily budget stays exhausted and the market braces for tonight's Applied Materials print (~11% implied move); Tail stays low while Stress builds toward the 20:00 UTC cash close
body: Roughly six hours after the 13:30 UTC cash open, web reporting confirms the Nasdaq-100 complex continues to hold its advance: the S&P 500 sits at a fresh record above 7,800 for the first time, and the Nasdaq Composite remains higher on the day with semiconductor-led breadth -- Sandisk and Micron both reported sharply higher earlier in the session -- alongside continued strength in megacap tech names. A flat July producer price index continues to reinforce Wednesday's benign CPI print and reduced Fed-hike odds heading into September. WTI crude held its recent slide, down roughly 1.4% to about $81-82/bbl. Alpha Vantage's free-tier daily request budget remains fully exhausted this run: a first-call TREASURY_YIELD (2-year) attempt returned an explicit rate_limit error, a single retry per the standing procedure returned the identical error, and no further Alpha Vantage calls were attempted to avoid wasting budget. Both the 2Y/10Y Treasury yield and QQQ GLOBAL_QUOTE therefore remain unconfirmed beyond Wednesday's close levels (10Y ~4.70% as of the August 11 reading, with August 13's release still pending) carried forward from prior runs. VIX likewise has no fresh Thursday print available via search and is carried forward near Wednesday's close (~14.4, a seven-month low), consistent with continued volatility compression but not independently confirmed intraday. Applied Materials reports fiscal Q3 results after today's close, with its call at 20:30 UTC (4:30pm ET); consensus expects roughly $9.0B revenue and $3.38 non-GAAP EPS, in line with management's own guidance midpoint, and the options market is now pricing an implied post-earnings move of approximately 11% in either direction -- nearly double the stock's roughly 6% average one-day move over the past four quarters, a meaningful amplifier for tonight's danger window. Iran's Hormuz standoff remains unresolved and unchanged in substance since the prior run: Iran's foreign minister said the U.S. has 'long miscalculated' over the strait, Iranian officials continue to dispute Trump's claim of 'total control,' and Hormuz transit traffic remains near three-month lows; no new kinetic escalation or market-transmission event has been identified. Given the continued advance with no observed failed-retracement or repeated-extension structure, and the absence of any new escalatory or macro shock, Tail holds at 16%, still low. Stress builds to 43% (from 38% last hour) as the session moves into its final hour before the 20:00 UTC close and tonight's unusually wide AMAT earnings reaction; it stays within the moderate band, just below the elevated threshold, since no new shock has actually printed yet. Confidence holds at 50% (essentially flat from 48%), reflecting a second consecutive Alpha Vantage rate-limit this run and Treasury/VIX levels still carried forward from Wednesday's close, partially offset by fresh, quantified web corroboration of the record S&P level, the oil decline, and the AMAT implied-move detail.

forecastDetail.comment: Roughly six hours into the cash session, the S&P 500 holds its fresh record above 7,800 with Nasdaq Composite/semiconductor leadership (Sandisk, Micron) intact and no observed failed-pullback structure; Alpha Vantage's free-tier daily budget remains fully exhausted (two rate-limited attempts this run), so this hour leans on web reporting alone and Stress ticks up toward the mid-40s into the approaching cash close.

The 20:00 UTC cash close coincides with Applied Materials' 20:30 UTC earnings call, where the options market is pricing an implied ~11% post-earnings move (versus a ~6% average over the last four quarters); Stress peaks for the day on this concentrated event/whipsaw risk, though pre-print alignment is not treated as already observed.

The AMAT after-hours reaction continues to resolve into the evening; Stress stays elevated within range until the initial post-earnings move is confirmed one way or the other, with no change yet to the low-Tail read.
As the post-earnings reaction settles and Asian trading has not yet opened, Stress eases back toward the day's lower range with no confirmed failed-retracement structure carried into the close.
Late-evening liquidity thins further with no confirmed AMAT-driven follow-through into the index; Stress continues easing toward the overnight low absent new catalysts.

Into the Asia/Europe overnight transition with thin liquidity and no confirmed one-way structure, Stress holds near its overnight low; the next material checkpoint is tomorrow's 12:30 UTC Retail Sales print.
